nutrients.name: Protein
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Protein quality varies by amino acid completeness; dairy, eggs, soy and whey provide complete profiles, while pulses and cereals complement each other.

nutrients.name: Dietary Fibre
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Natural dietary fibre from whole grains, legumes and seeds promotes satiety and healthy glycemic response.

nutrients.name: Carbohydrates
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Complex carbohydrates provide steady sustained energy compared to rapid glucose spikes from refined sugars.

nutrients.name: Total Fat
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Dietary lipids support fat-soluble vitamin absorption (A, D, E, K); unsaturated fats are preferable.

nutrients.name: Calcium
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Dairy calcium typically exhibits 30-35% bioavailability, whereas plant phytates/oxalates may modulate absorption.

nutrients.name: Potassium
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Essential intracellular electrolyte assisting in vascular relaxation and counteracting excess sodium.

nutrients.name: Phosphorus
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Works synergistically with calcium for skeletal mineralization; abundant in dairy and grain seeds.

nutrients.name: Iron
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Non-heme plant iron has lower absorption (5-12%) than heme iron, but co-ingestion of Vitamin C significantly boosts uptake.

nutrients.name: Magnesium
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Crucial enzyme cofactor for muscle, nerve transmission, and energy metabolism.

nutrients.name: Zinc
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Bioavailability is elevated in fermented/leavened foods where phytates are degraded.

nutrients.name: Vitamin A
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Must be declared in µg Retinol Activity Equivalents (RAE); fortification must be declared on package.

nutrients.name: Vitamin B1 (Thiamine)
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Water-soluble coenzyme in carbohydrate metabolism; heat-sensitive during high-temperature baking.

nutrients.name: Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Essential for cellular energy production; naturally gives milk whey its golden-greenish tint.

nutrients.name: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Stable micronutrient assisting DNA repair and cellular respiration.

nutrients.name: Vitamin B6
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Facilitates amino acid metabolism, neurotransmitter synthesis, and hemoglobin formation.

nutrients.name: Vitamin E
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Lipid-soluble antioxidant protecting cell membranes; absorption dependent on presence of dietary fats.

nutrients.name: Folate (Vitamin B9)
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Vital for red blood cell formation and healthy cellular division; synthetic folic acid has higher bioavailability than food folates.

nutrients.name: Vitamin B12
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Naturally occurring almost exclusively in animal and dairy foods; crucial for neuro-cognitive health.

nutrients.name: Vitamin D
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Fat-soluble vitamin directing intestinal calcium absorption; frequently added via certified milk/oil fortification (+F).

nutrients.name: Vitamin C
nutrients.bioavailabilityNote: Potent antioxidant and cofactor for collagen synthesis; boosts dietary non-heme iron absorption.
